newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian assistant treasurer resigns over shares.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian assistant treasurer resigns over shares.

text.p: Australian assistant treasurer Jim Short, the junior minister responsible for banking policy, resigned on Sunday following controversy over his ownership of shares in a major bank, Prime Minister John Howard announced.
"The assistant treasurer, Senator Jim Short, has tendered his resignation from the ministry," Howard said in a statement.
"I have accepted that resignation," he said.
Howard last week said he had considered sacking Short for failing to reveal that his family company held shares in Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd (ANZ).
Howard said then that he had decided not to sack Short for breaching ministerial guidelines because he considered the holding of the shares to be an oversight.

However, more information came to light on the weekend when Short later told Howard that his office had discovered that in June he had granted a routine approval for a banking license for an ANZ subsidiary.
"Now that my attention has been drawn to that approval, I feel that the circumstances of the matter have changed," Short said in a resignation letter released by Howard.
Howard said on Sunday: "At all times he has behaved with honesty and integrity. Not even his harshest critics in recent days have said that he lacked either of these qualities."
Short said last week he had taken steps to dispose of his 6,679 shares, worth about A$48,000 based on Friday's closing price on the stock exchange.

Under the ministerial guidelines drawn up by Howard's government, ministers are required to divest themselves of all shares and similar interests in any company or business involved in the area of their portfolio responsibilities.
Howard said Short's position in the ministry would be taken by Rod Kemp, a senator from Victoria and brother of David Kemp, junior minister for schools, vocational education and training.
